issues.issue: The definition operates entirely by reference to a blank form heading ("the person identified under the heading 'Customer' above"), which on this unexecuted form identifies no one.

The defined "we/us" is a single Texas entity, but the arbitration section (c073) expands "we" and "us" to affiliates and the opt-out notice (c094) is addressed to a different entity, PLS Financial Services.
The Lender is identified as a non-party, yet the arbitration and jury-waiver provisions (c052, c074) purport to bind and benefit "Lender" as though it were a contracting party.
The disclaimer of any lender or fiduciary role sits uneasily with the LOC and reimbursement obligations (c033–c038) under which CAB pays the lender and is repaid with 10% per annum interest.
The obligation is only to "attempt to" obtain a loan, issue the LOC and assist with documents, leaving the standard of performance for the fee undefined.
A one-day estimated performance period is hard to square with c008/c009, which describe reminder, education, check-cashing and branch-network services provided "throughout the term".

The listed additional services are hedged by "attempt to", "upon request", "where available" and "certain CAB services", so it is unclear what, if anything, is actually promised in return for the fee.
"The term" is not a defined period anywhere in this Agreement, and "may be provided" leaves it uncertain whether the additional services are promised at all.

"Denied by the Lender" is the only stated no-fee condition, while c021 says the CAB fee is "earned in advance at the inception of the loan"; the two must be harmonised for applications never acted on.
"Not open-ended in nature" is a conclusory characterisation with no operative content, and its meaning must be supplied from elsewhere.
The clause says the CAB fee "is not interest" yet must be included in the finance charge, an internal characterisation a party could argue cuts both ways on usury.
The rate is left as a garbled blank ("upon °% annualized rate"), so the central price term of the agreement is unstated on its face.
"Earned in advance at the inception of the loan" is in tension with c027, which entitles the customer to a prorated daily refund of part of the CAB fee on payment in full.
Every numeric term (loan amount, number of payments, Amount Financed, Finance Charge) is left blank and the sentence is truncated mid-phrase.
The amounts are blank and the text is garbled and truncated ("our CAB fee for this transaction ofS"), leaving the composition of the finance charge unstated.
The APR, payment dates, payment amounts and Total of Payments are all blank, so the payment schedule cannot be applied from the text.
The single payment-application waterfall covers late charges and returned item fees that c032 says are owed to the Lender rather than to CAB, leaving it unclear whose payments are being allocated.
"A refund of part of the CAB fee based on a prorated daily basis for the final period" does not say what "the final period" is or how the refund is computed.
The charge list ends with the open-ended "attorneys' fees, and costs of collection" appended to specific dollar items, leaving the reach of the catch-all uncertain.
The placement of "if payment is 10 or more days late" leaves it arguable whether the condition qualifies only the late charge or the whole list of lender charges.
The LOC is described as "irrevocable", yet c037 provides that it is "automatically revoked" on a timely cancellation and c036 fixes an expiry date.
The lender's bare statement of default suffices for payment even though c039 disclaims any duty to verify it, while c043 defines default by reference to the customer's own conduct.
Automatic revocation on cancellation cannot easily be squared with c033's statement that the LOC issued to the lender is "irrevocable" under Chapter 5 of the Texas Business and Commerce Code.

The disclaimer of responsibility for the accuracy of the lender's default statement sits against c034/c044, under which the customer is charged with reimbursing whatever CAB pays on that unverified statement.
The sentence is mangled ("unlgyuful excess", "reduced to the maximug peepee law"), so the savings mechanism it states cannot be read as written.
The sentence breaks off mid-word ("calculate charges by amortiz"), leaving the permitted method of computing charges incomplete.
Default limb (2), "if you fail to perform your other promises to us", is unbounded and could be triggered by any minor undertaking, including the certifications in c118–c120.
"We may exercise any other right or remedy allowed by law" is a catch-all appended to the single specific remedy of collecting a check, leaving its reach uncertain.

The right to "seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us" is in tension with c064, which forbids threatening or pursuing criminal charges related to a check given as security for a loan.
An anti-waiver clause preserving delayed enforcement bears on whether PLS could still demand arbitration after acting inconsistently with it (c074, c075), a point a court would have to reconcile.
"We are not required to file suit or arbitrate" is hard to reconcile with c071/c074, under which any Claim "shall be resolved by binding arbitration" upon either party's election.
The Agreement elsewhere refers only to a check or similar payment device and never grants a security interest, so "any collateral" has no referent in the instrument.
Permission to "sue or arbitrate with one or more persons without joining" others must be read against c106's flat prohibition on joinder or consolidation in any arbitration.
A jury-trial waiver binding "Lender" is difficult to square with c004, which identifies the Lender as a third party that is not a signatory to this Agreement.
The clause speaks of not "reject[ing]" the Arbitration Agreement, while the arbitration section (c093) provides only an "opt out" mechanism, so the trigger is described by an undefined term.

If the arbitration agreement is rejected, this clause leaves the jury waiver operative even though c098 assumes no jury trial only when arbitration is chosen; the interaction with c093–c096 is unresolved.
This compliance savings language duplicates c040 in the LOC section, with slightly different wording covering different actors, raising the usual question of which governs.
The clause restates c041 (the garbled unlawful-excess savings clause in the LOC section) in different terms, so the two savings provisions must be reconciled.
"Amortizing, prorating, allocating and spreading" is left without an object or method, so what may be spread and over what period is unstated.

"Any claim that this agreement or related matter, or any action or inaction by us or Lender, or by any other person, is legally non-compliant, illegal or unenforceable" is drafted so broadly and one-sidedly that its coverage and its status as a condition precedent are open to construction.

A mandatory 60-day pre-suit notice sits awkwardly with c075, which lets either party demand arbitration of a Claim "at any time", and with the arbitration section's silence on any notice-and-cure condition.
Notice to the Lender is directed to PLS's own Chicago legal department, which conflicts with c004's identification of DSI Lending Resources as a separate third-party lender.
"Any corrective action shall relieve us and Lender of any liability" does not say what corrective action suffices or whether it must actually cure the claim.

"Reasonable attorneys' fees ... regardless of whether legal proceedings are actually filed, and all costs and disbursements" leaves both the reasonableness measure and the scope of "all costs and disbursements" open.

"A person may not threaten or pursue criminal charges" does not say who is bound or whether it creates any contractual promise by PLS, and the exception ends in the open catch-all "or other criminal conduct" after forgery, fraud and theft.

The restriction on pursuing criminal charges over a check given as security is in direct tension with c044, which gives PLS the right on default to "seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us" and any other remedy allowed by law.
"You and we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court" is stated as an unconditional commitment, though the mechanism that follows is elective and revocable.

The flat agreement to arbitrate instead of litigating cannot be squared with c074/c075 (arbitration only "upon the election" of a party, even after a lawsuit is begun), c047 ("we are not required to ... arbitrate") and the opt-out in c093.

"Claim" sweeps in "the actions of you, us, Lender, or third parties" and "any products or services offered to you", a boundless catch-all beside the specific enumerated agreements, and limb (e) purports to delegate the validity of the arbitration agreement itself.

The exclusion in limb (i) for loans "in connection with which you properly exercised an opt-out right" must be read against c096, which excludes only claims "arising under this Agreement", leaving the opt-out's reach unresolved.

Expanding "we" and "us" to affiliates, agents and owners for arbitration purposes conflicts with the c003 definition limiting those words to PLS Loan Store of Texas, Inc., and determines whether non-signatories may compel arbitration.
Arbitration arises only "upon the election" of a party, yet the same sentence says any Claim "shall be resolved by binding arbitration", mixing permissive and mandatory language.
The election mechanism sits against c071's unconditional "we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court", so whether arbitration is automatic or must be invoked is contestable.

"At any time, even if the other party has begun a lawsuit" says nothing about conduct short of a lawsuit and does not address whether the right to demand arbitration can be waived by inconsistent litigation conduct.
Read with c046 (delay in enforcing rights does not lose them) and c076 (no arbitration after judgment), the provision leaves unclear whether invoking other legal processes forfeits arbitration.
"Matters included in the judgment" and "a lawsuit involving you, us, or Lender" leave uncertain which prior proceedings, including criminal or third-party proceedings, cut off the arbitration right.

After naming two specific organizations the clause adds "any other arbitrator ... reasonably satisfactory to us", a general catch-all controlled by one party, and it conflates selecting an arbitration organization with selecting an individual arbitrator.

This clause forfeits the customer's right for failing to select "an arbitrator" within 20 days, whereas c077 gives the customer the right to select an arbitration organization, and c079 assumes the parties must "agree" on an arbitrator.
"If we are not able to agree on another arbitrator" does not say with whom agreement is required, and "the named organization" has no clear antecedent given the list in c077.
Defaulting to the AAA Rules for Consumer Arbitrations may be inoperative because c081 and c107 bar selecting any organization whose rules permit class arbitration or reject the class waiver.

"Permits class actions in arbitration" is untested against organizations whose rules neither authorise nor forbid them, and it duplicates but does not match c107's "does not accept this class action waiver".
The cap is measured by "what your court costs would have been if the Claim had been resolved in a state court with jurisdiction", a hypothetical figure the clause gives no method for calculating.
The FAA choice must be read with c110, which applies Texas law to the Agreement generally but the FAA to the arbitration agreement, and with c087's direction that the arbitrator "apply relevant law".
Three alternative venues are listed without saying who chooses among them, and "such other location as we or Lender may agree" does not identify with whom agreement is needed.

Directing the arbitrator to "apply relevant law" while forbidding federal or state rules of procedure or evidence leaves it unclear how substantive law with embedded procedural content is to be applied.
The contemplation of a possible in-person hearing must be read against c086's venue rule, which assumes a hearing "at which you must appear in person".
Each party bearing its own attorneys' fees is in tension with c063 and c031, which make the customer liable for PLS's attorneys' fees and costs of collection.
The deeming provision fixes the place of the award by the customer's "home address" at the time of the decision, which may be nowhere connected to the arbitration venue set by c086.
The opt-out right for "Claims arising under this Agreement" is narrower than the c072 definition of Claim, which reaches prior agreements, other products and the actions of third parties.
The opt-out notice must be sent to "PLS Financial Services", an entity that is not the defined "we/us" in c003 and not the addressee for notices under c060.
"Arising under this Agreement" is a narrower formula than the "arising from or relating to" language defining Claim, so the effect of an opt-out on the wider class of Claims is uncertain.

The limitation cannot readily be squared with c072, which defines Claim to include disputes about prior agreements, other products and third-party actions, all of which the opt-out apparently leaves arbitrable.

Making prior and subsequent transactions arbitrable under their own agreements is difficult to reconcile with c072(b), which folds any prior credit services agreement or loan into the Claims covered here.
The statement that neither party can litigate a Claim once arbitration is chosen sits against c075, which permits an arbitration demand even after a lawsuit has begun, and c076's judgment carve-out.
The waiver is conditioned on someone choosing arbitration ("If either you, we, or Lender ... choose arbitration"), while c101–c104 state the class waiver unconditionally.
The absolute bar on participating in any class action is stated without the "if arbitration is chosen" condition that qualifies the same waiver in c100.
"In any other representative capacity for others" is a catch-all following the specific examples of class representative and private attorney general, leaving its reach uncertain.

An absolute bar on joinder or consolidation is in tension with c050, under which PLS "may sue or arbitrate with one or more persons", and with c052/c074 treating the non-signatory Lender as an arbitration participant.
This organization-eligibility rule overlaps but does not match c081's differently worded exclusion, and both may disqualify the AAA default supplied by c080.
This arbitration-specific severability clause does not match the general severability-and-reformation clause in c115, and neither says which controls if the class waiver falls.

The carve-out making the arbitration agreement subject only to the FAA must be reconciled with c087 (arbitrator applies relevant law) and c085, leaving the source of law governing arbitrability and unconscionability contestable.

An integration clause limited to "the subject matter of this Agreement" is hard to apply given the separate Credit Services Disclosure Statement acknowledged in c116 and the separate loan documents with the Lender.
A signed-writing requirement for modification is in tension with c018, which contemplates refinancing on new documents, and with c046, which lets PLS waive rights without losing them.
"Reformed if practicable so as to achieve its intended purpose(s)" gives no standard for practicability or for identifying the intended purpose.
This reformation-based severability clause differs from the arbitration-specific severability rule in c108, which simply preserves the remainder without reformation.
The acknowledgment that the Agreement was received "WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED" cannot be squared with c020–c024, whose price and payment blanks are unfilled.
Certifying agreement to "the binding Arbitration Agreement" at signature is in tension with c093, which allows the customer 30 days after signing to opt out of arbitration entirely.
The warranty of "no intention to file a petition for relief" turns on the customer's undisclosed state of mind, which the clause gives no way to test.

The sentence is ungrammatical ("the account on which any check ... that you provide to us is drawn, is a legitimate, open, and active account") and "legitimate" is undefined, which matters because a false warranty here bears on the criminal-conduct exception in c064.

The warranty of an open and active account interacts with c064's prohibition on pursuing criminal charges absent "forgery, fraud, theft, or other criminal conduct", since PLS could treat a returned check as a breach of this warranty.

"Any information you provide to us or that we obtain from third parties" shared "for the duration of the services or any subsequent services" leaves both the scope of the information and the duration unbounded.
The cancellation deadline runs from "the date of the transaction", whereas the attached Notice of Cancellation (c123) measures the same three days from the date the contract is signed.

"Within three days after the date the contract is signed" does not match c122's "before midnight of the third day after the date of the transaction", leaving two different deadlines in the same instrument.
The promise to return "any payment made by you under this contract" within 10 days is in tension with c021, which says the CAB fee is earned in advance at the inception of the loan.
The operative deadline is left blank ("not later than midnight on"), so the notice form states no date by which cancellation must be delivered.
